targets.old_statement: Bald tires stretch stops and fight turns on wet roads, so check pressure against the manual or door jamb monthly and before long trips.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Bald tires stretch stops and fight turns on wet roads, so check pressure against the manual or door jamb monthly and before long trips.
targets.statement: Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance and make wet turns harder, so check tire pressure with a gauge against the owner's manual or driver's door jamb recommendation, and inspect tires for wear and damage monthly and before long road trips.

targets.old_statement: The penny test parks Lincoln head first in the tread groove: covered crown means safe rubber, bare head means replace.
targets.old_spoken_statement: The penny test parks Lincoln head first in the tread groove: covered crown means safe rubber, bare head means replace.
targets.statement: For the penny test, place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves where tread looks lowest: if any part of Lincoln's head is covered by tread, tread depth is safe, whereas lower tread greatly reduces road grip in adverse conditions.

targets.old_statement: Any age driver may call out emergencies to responders, hospitals, clinics and police or fire outfits, and adult peace, fire and ambulance crews may use handhelds on duty.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Any age driver may call out emergencies to responders, hospitals, clinics and police or fire outfits, and adult peace, fire and ambulance crews may use handhelds on duty.
targets.statement: In an emergency, a driver of any age may use a cell phone or mobile electronic device to call police or fire departments, an ambulance service, a hospital, a health clinic, a physician's office, or an emergency response operator, while peace officers, firefighters, and ambulance drivers eighteen or older may use handheld devices.
